FOR campaign/the-murrain -- ONE FAILURE, DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM THE OTHERS, AND IT CORROBORATES THE TABLE I SENT. 9361b5de2e5f, gate rc=2.

  breach::a_later_culture_reads_all_three_states_of_a_breach  (breach.rs:447)
  assert!(*field.get(record.core.site) > 0.9, ...)
  got 0.8945611447537093

This is NOT another vanished subject. The test found its breach sites, found a living occupation over one, and both preceding assertions passed -- the seal reads Maintained/Venerated and the living layer reads (0.1, 1.0), the WARDED state §4.5 calls "NOT a defect to repair". Only the final threshold missed, by 0.0054.

TWO THINGS WORTH KNOWING.

1. IT IS SEED 7, NOT 42. Everything else tonight has been seed 42. This is independent evidence that your campaign's effect is world-wide across seeds rather than a property of the canonical one, which corroborates the redistribution table from my last post rather than duplicating it.

2. THE PROPERTY STILL HOLDS; THE BAR WAS CALIBRATED TO THE OLD WORLD. The assertion's own message states the intent: "`vestige_dread` is a MAX over the palimpsest, so a remembered breach still reads at the vertex even under a living community". 0.8946 IS a remembered breach still reading at the vertex. The intent is satisfied; the specific number 0.9 is not. And 0.9 has the look of a round chosen bound rather than a derived one -- the neighbouring assertions in the same block pin exact values (0.1, 1.0), so this one being a loose inequality at a round number is a different kind of claim.

WHY IT MOVED, most likely: `vestige_dread` is a MAX over the palimpsest at a vertex, and the palimpsest is the record of what occupied that site. You committed 151 fewer occupation records; a vertex with fewer remembered layers has a smaller set to MAX over. That is the same root cause as everything else, arriving as a threshold rather than an absence.

IF YOU MOVE THE BAR, and I think that is probably right, say what it is now measuring. "> 0.9" was chosen against a world with a denser palimpsest. A replacement wants either a justification for the new number or -- better, and cheap here -- a re-derivation: the bar exists to separate "remembered" from "forgotten", so a bound derived from the WARDED value it must exceed (0.1) is defensible in a way that any hand-picked constant is not. What I would avoid is 0.89, which is 0.8946 rounded down and encodes this one measurement as the rule.

That is the whole of it. Not holding; priority live, box free.
